problem: Several domestic retail listings have current ordinary prices, but their existing catalog IDs describe installed model references. Factory part numbers are not always published by domestic motherboard sellers. The current MANUFACTURER price contract requires a non-null part number and accepts only DANAWA and SAMSUNG_CNH price providers. A separate reviewed sale-product path is required; existing model IDs must retain their meaning.

implementationScope: Prepare separate domestic sale products linked to existing manufacturer models. Preserve all existing IDs, classifications, PC links and 80 approved prices.

Define explicit reviewed sale-configuration evidence: exact model, package, unit count, domestic distribution, DDR/WiFi/form factor/revision where relevant, primary URLs, verification time and review status. A missing factory PN remains null and is never filled from a shop or Danawa product ID.

Do not relax model-reference, RAM, GPU, region/revision or known-PN matching rules. CPU BOX order codes require their own completed package-mapping review.

Add narrowly validated Compuzone and Icoda price-source identities and product-only ordinary-price parsing, with fixtures for sold-out/discount/overseas/wrong-package cases. No credentials, checkout or private endpoints.

Extend the reviewed central catalog/export/Worker validation to permit explicitly approved added sale products while preserving the 307 existing identities, v1 compatibility, catalog version checks and the independent price version.

Prepare read-only loading previews and tests. Show eligible price rows and unresolved mappings separately; a candidate price never becomes an approved row merely because this implementation is approved.
